title: Stability of wearing-position bias with sample size
text:
The metric comparison established that wearing position (chest and wrist, relative to the glasses reference) introduces outcome-level bias in personal light-exposure metrics. This notebook asks a complementary, design-oriented question:

How does the precision of the estimated bias change as participants and participant-days accumulate?

The analysis includes every metric with daily observations. Interdaily stability (IS) and intradaily variability (IV) are excluded because they are defined across multiple days and therefore have no participant-day estimates. The remaining metrics are summarized by the six metric classes used in the primary analysis: duration, exposure history, level, spectrum, temporal dynamics, and timing.
Two bootstrap axes are evaluated for both chest and wrist:

N participants: sample 1–200 participants, with either 3 or 7 days per sampled participant.
Days per participant: sample 1–7 days per participant in studies with either 25 or 50 participants.

At each sample size, the standard deviation (SD) of the bootstrapped mean bias quantifies sampling uncertainty. Bias is calculated on each metric’s model scale and normalized to the absolute mean glasses reference on that scale. The normalized SDs are then summarized pointwise by their median within each metric class. A 5% SD is used as a practical precision tolerance.

text:
Setup and inputs



Setup

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(LightLogR)
library(cowplot)
library(gt)
library(here)
library(webshot2)

here::i_am("notebooks/JZ_error_stabilisation.qmd")

if (packageVersion("LightLogR") < package_version("0.10.3")) {
  stop("This analysis requires LightLogR 0.10.3 or newer.", call. = FALSE)
}


The prepared long-format metric data and their model metadata are loaded from the same sources used by the metric-comparison notebook. The reusable bootstrap helpers are kept in a separate script so the sampling and aggregation logic can be tested independently.



Import metrics, metadata, and helpers

load(here("data/prepared_metrics.RData"))
metric_info <- read_xlsx(here("data/metric_types.xlsx"))
source(here("scripts/bootstrap_stability.R"))


A single seed makes all bootstrap scenarios reproducible. The source notebook defaults to 10,000 draws for production. The draw count is a parameter so a render can be tested quickly with, for example, quarto render notebooks/_JZ_error_stabilisation.qmd --execute -P draws:100.



Analysis settings

production_draws <- 10000L
draws <- as.integer(params$draws)
if (length(draws) != 1L || is.na(draws) || draws < 2L) {
  stop("`params$draws` must be one integer greater than one.", call. = FALSE)
}

days_per_participant <- c(3L, 7L)
day_axis_participants <- c(25L, 50L)
tolerance <- 5

bootstrap_input_paths <- c(
  prepared_metrics = here("data/prepared_metrics.RData"),
  metric_types = here("data/metric_types.xlsx"),
  bootstrap_helpers = here("scripts/bootstrap_stability.R")
)
bootstrap_input_checksums <- setNames(
  unname(tools::md5sum(bootstrap_input_paths)),
  names(bootstrap_input_paths)
)
bootstrap_cache_key <- list(
  draws = draws,
  days_per_participant = days_per_participant,
  day_axis_participants = day_axis_participants,
  input_checksums = bootstrap_input_checksums
)

set.seed(7391)

position_colors <- ggsci::pal_jco()(3) |>
  set_names(c("glasses", "chest", "wrist"))

metric_class_labels <- c(
  duration = "Duration",
  `exposure history` = "Exposure history",
  level = "Level",
  spectrum = "Spectrum",
  `temporal dynamics` = "Temporal dynamics",
  timing = "Timing"
)


This production render uses B = 10,000 bootstrap draws.

text:
Bootstrap design
Both axes use hierarchical resampling with replacement. For the participant axis, each bootstrap replicate samples \(N\) participants and then samples exactly 3 or 7 valid paired days from each selected participant’s empirical daily-bias distribution. For the participant-day axis, each replicate first samples 25 or 50 participants and then samples 1–7 days from each. Sampling days with replacement retains participants with fewer observed valid days while making the target design size explicit.
The participant axis extends to 200 as an empirical-distribution projection, although the prepared cohort contains 106 participants. It therefore describes expected sampling precision under repeated sampling from this cohort’s empirical distribution, not the acquisition of new independent population information.



Bootstrap all daily metrics and four design scenarios

metric_stability <- bootstrap_stability(
  bias_df,
  n_range = 1:200,
  day_range = 1:7,
  B = draws,
  days_per_participant = days_per_participant,
  day_axis_participants = day_axis_participants
)

text:
Stabilisation figure
The eight panels cross wearing position (rows) with the four design scenarios (columns). Faint colored lines show every daily metric, while the thicker lines show their pointwise metric-class medians. The dashed line marks the 5% SD tolerance. In each leftmost facet, right-aligned direct labels and arrows identify the three individual metrics with the largest SD at 200 participants. The first two columns vary participants from 1 to 200 with 3 or 7 days each. The final two vary days per participant from 1 to 7 with 25 or 50 participants. To preserve detail around the tolerance, the display is clipped at 20%; larger SDs remain in the analysis.



Metric-class stability by design scenario

fig_stability <- plot_stability(
  metric_stability,
  class_stability,
  position_colors = position_colors,
  metric_class_labels = metric_class_labels,
  tol = tolerance,
  ylim = c(0, 20),
  draws = draws
)

text:
Sample size at the 5% tolerance
For every class, position, and design scenario, the table reports the first sample size at which the class-median SD is at or below 5%. A dash means the tolerance is not reached within 1–200 participants or 1–7 days per participant. The crossing applies to the class median and does not imply that every individual metric in that class has crossed the tolerance.



Class-median sample size to reach 5 percent SD

crossing_wide <- crossing_table(class_stability, tol = tolerance) |>
  mutate(
    metric_class = factor(
      metric_class,
      levels = names(metric_class_labels),
      labels = unname(metric_class_labels)
    ),
    scenario_code = case_when(
      boot_type == "participants" & days_per_participant == 3L ~ "p3",
      boot_type == "participants" & days_per_participant == 7L ~ "p7",
      boot_type == "participant-days" & n_participants == 25L ~ "d25",
      boot_type == "participant-days" & n_participants == 50L ~ "d50",
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    position = str_to_lower(position),
    output_column = paste(scenario_code, position, sep = "_")
  ) |>
  select(metric_class, n_metrics, output_column, n_within) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = output_column, values_from = n_within) |>
  arrange(metric_class)

title: Stability of wearing-position bias with sample size
text:
Interpretation
The figure isolates precision rather than bias magnitude. Increasing the number of participants reduces uncertainty in the estimated population mean, whereas adding days primarily reduces within-participant sampling uncertainty and is ultimately limited by between-participant heterogeneity. The paired 3- versus 7-day participant scenarios show how much of the participant-axis precision is attributable to longer monitoring. Likewise, the 25- versus 50-participant day scenarios show how study size changes the value of additional days.
The thick class medians provide a concise design summary across all daily metrics, while the faint individual traces expose metric-level heterogeneity. The class medians should therefore be used to compare broad metric classes, not to choose a sample size for a single specific metric. The direct labels in the leftmost facets identify the three metrics with the largest SD at the maximum participant sample size; they are not a separate inferential comparison. A small SD indicates that the placement bias is estimated precisely; it does not indicate that the placement bias itself is small.

title: Preparation of metrics for participant-day analyses - wake-only sensitivity
text:
This document prepares a wake-only sensitivity dataset from the same primary-analysis participant-day sample used in JZ_metric_preparation.qmd. The existing 50% hourly and 80% daily completeness checks are applied before diary-defined sleep is removed, so planned sleep does not make a day fail a 24-hour completeness rule. Immediately before metrics are calculated, measurements are set to missing during documented non-wear and diary-defined sleep. Pre-sleep time is retained, and absent state information is treated as undocumented rather than inferred.
The wake-only estimand is each participant-day’s light exposure during valid, concurrent waking wear at the glasses, chest, and wrist positions. Timestamps and missing epochs are preserved. Missing periods therefore break threshold episodes and cannot be mistaken for darkness or silently join measurements from opposite sides of sleep or non-wear.
Forty-two metrics are retained. Interdaily stability, intradaily variability, nvRD, the four darkest-10-hour outcomes, the three dark Barroso outcomes, circadian variation, and disparity index are excluded. frequency_crossing_250 is retained using a gap-aware implementation. Brightest-10-hour and bright Barroso outcomes are interpreted conditionally on available valid waking-wear observations, not as complete 24-hour light schedules.

sleepprep is used as the start of the sleep interval because this is when the device positions were set for the night. The derived Brown sleep state is used to distinguish sleep from pre-sleep and waking time.

text:
This document collects the raw light exposure data for all three wearing positions through the melidosData package. In this sensitivity scenario, documented non-wear and diary-defined sleep are retained. The data are preprocessed to

An unaggregated set of light exposure data, both for the eye-level and chest-level wearing position where


Values > 100 000 lx are removed (set to NA)
remove observations where not all three wearing positions are available


A further processed set (from 1.) where


hours with less than 50% data availability are removed
days with less than 80% data availability (after the previous step) are removed

With the cleaned dataset, metrics per participant and day are calculated (with explicit exceptions). The resulting dataset is the basis for downstream inferential analyses.

Create convenience function for converting datetime to time to double

#| label: datetime-conversion-helper
#| filename: Create convenience function for converting datetime to time to double
datetime_2_numeric <- function(x) {
  x |> 
    mutate(
      across(
        where(is.POSIXct),
        \(x) x |> hms::as_hms() %>% as.numeric()
      )
    )
}





Prepare metrics data

#| label: prepare-metrics-data
#| filename: Prepare metrics data
metrics_data <-
  light_fin |> 
  distinct(site, Id, Datetime, .keep_all = TRUE) |> 
    pivot_longer(MEDI_glasses:LIGHT_wrist,
                 names_sep = "_",
                 names_to = c("metric", "position")) |> 
    pivot_wider(values_from = value, names_from = metric)





Calculate by-day metrics

#| label: calculate-daily-metrics
#| filename: Calculate by-day metrics
#| warning: false
metrics <- 
  metrics_data |> 
  group_by(site, Id, Date, position) |> 
        summarize(
          duration_above_threshold(
            MEDI, Datetime, "above", 10, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE),
          duration_above_threshold(
            MEDI, Datetime, "above", 250, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE),
          duration_above_threshold(
            MEDI, Datetime, "above", 1000, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE),
          period_above_threshold(
            MEDI, Datetime, "above", 10, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE),
          period_above_threshold(
            MEDI, Datetime, "above", 250, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE),
          period_above_threshold(
            MEDI, Datetime, "above", 1000, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE),
          pulses_above_threshold(
            MEDI, Datetime, threshold = 250, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE
          )|>
            datetime_2_numeric(),
          pulses_above_threshold(
            MEDI, Datetime, threshold = 1000, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE
          )|>
            datetime_2_numeric(),
          bright_dark_period(
                  MEDI |> log_zero_inflated(),
                  Datetime, "brightest", "10 hours",
                  as.df = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE
                  ) %>%
            datetime_2_numeric(),
          bright_dark_period(
                  MEDI |> log_zero_inflated(),
                  Datetime, "darkest", "10 hours", as.df = TRUE,
                  loop = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE
                  ) %>%
            datetime_2_numeric(),
          timing_above_threshold(
              MEDI, Datetime, "above", 10, as.df = TRUE) |>
            datetime_2_numeric(),
          timing_above_threshold(MEDI, Datetime, "above", 250, as.df = TRUE) |>
            datetime_2_numeric(),
          frequency_crossing_threshold(MEDI, 250, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE),
          timing_above_threshold(
              MEDI, Datetime, "above", 1000, as.df = TRUE) |>
            datetime_2_numeric(),
          barroso_lighting_metrics(
            MEDI, Datetime, loop = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE
             ),
          centroidLE(MEDI, Datetime, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE) |>
            datetime_2_numeric(),
          disparity_index(MEDI, TRUE, TRUE),
          midpointCE(MEDI, Datetime, TRUE, TRUE)|>
            datetime_2_numeric(),
          mean_MEDI = mean(MEDI |> log_zero_inflated(), na.rm = TRUE),
          nvRD = nvRD(MEDI, LIGHT, Datetime) |> mean(na.rm = TRUE),
          dose(MEDI, Datetime, na.rm = TRUE, as.df = TRUE),
          MDER = median(MEDI / LIGHT, na.rm = TRUE),
          .groups = "drop",
        ) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.duration), as.numeric)) %>% 
        pivot_longer(cols = -c(site, Id, Date, position), names_to = "metric")

title: Preparation of metrics for participant-day analyses
text:
This document collects the raw light exposure data for all three wearing positions through the melidosData package. This primary scenario removes documented non-wear outside diary-defined sleep while retaining sleep-time measurements. The data are preprocessed to

An unaggregated set of light exposure data, both for the eye-level and chest-level wearing position where


Values > 100 000 lx are removed (set to NA)
non-wear periods, that are not also sleep periods, are removed
remove observations where not all three wearing positions are available


A further processed set (from 1.) where


hours with less than 50% data availability are removed
days with less than 80% data availability (after the previous step) are removed

With the cleaned dataset, metrics per participant and day are calculated (with explicit exceptions). The resulting dataset is the basis for downstream inferential analyses.

Importing data

Light
In the first step, we import the unaggregated light eposure data for the glasses, chest, and wrist. These will be loaded from the GitHub project page. These data have been imported already, trimmed by trial dates, checked for irregular data and gaps. All of them run on a 10 second interval.



Import light data

light_glasses <- load_data("light_glasses")
light_chest <- load_data("light_chest")
light_wrist <- load_data("light_wrist")





Count participants and participant-days

light_glasses |> flatten_data() |> group_by(Id) |> n_groups()


[1] 143

light_chest |> flatten_data() |> group_by(Id) |> n_groups()

[1] 157

light_wrist |> flatten_data() |> group_by(Id) |> n_groups()

[1] 153

light_glasses |> flatten_data() |> group_by(Id) |> add_Date_col(group.by = TRUE) |> n_groups()

[1] 1136

light_chest |> flatten_data() |> group_by(Id) |> add_Date_col(group.by = TRUE) |> n_groups()

[1] 1249

light_wrist |> flatten_data() |> group_by(Id) |> add_Date_col(group.by = TRUE) |> n_groups()

[1] 1223




Sleep
The sleep data comes from a morning sleep diary. They contain both sleep and wake times.



Import sleep data

sleepdiary <- load_data("sleepdiaries")




Wear log
The non-wear data comes from an app-based wear log that participants filled in whenever they removed or put on the device(s).



Import wearlog data

wearlog <- load_data("wearlog")




Combine wearing positions

Only a selection of variables will be kept, namely MEDI (melanopic EDI) and LIGHT (photopic illuminance).
Other contextual variables that are kept are Id, Datetime, and position.
We further remove the MPI site from the glasses dataset, as no chest or wrist1 data were collected.
Then we will combine the observations of the wearing positions.
Lastly, we will calculate the photoperiod information for each site.




Remove MPI site

light_glasses$MPI <- NULL





Select relevant columns, combine positions, add photoperiod

light <-
  imap(
    light_glasses,
    \(data, idx) data |>
      select(Id, Datetime, MEDI, LIGHT) |> 
      data2reference(light_chest[[idx]], Reference.column = MEDI_chest) |> 
      data2reference(light_chest[[idx]],
                     Data.column = LIGHT,
                     Reference.column = LIGHT_chest) |> 
      data2reference(light_wrist[[idx]], Reference.column = MEDI_wrist) |>
      data2reference(light_wrist[[idx]],
                     Data.column = LIGHT,
                     Reference.column = LIGHT_wrist) |>
      add_photoperiod(melidos_coordinates[[idx]]) |> 
      rename(MEDI_glasses = MEDI, LIGHT_glasses = LIGHT)
  )

Note: the displayed warnings refer to the fact that participant FUSPCEU_S014 had a measurement interval of 60 seconds on the glasses, compared to the 10 seconds of everyone else (and both the other wearing positions). Thus, six measurement values from the chest and wrist positions map to one from the glasses. This is not deemed problematic, as it is only one participant in one site. The last of the six respective chest and wrist measurements will be used for comparison.



Remove instances with less than all wearing positions



Remove instances with less than all wearing positions

light <- 
  light |> 
  map(
    \(data) data |> 
              mutate(
                across(MEDI_glasses:LIGHT_wrist,
                \(x) {
                ifelse(is.na(MEDI_glasses) | is.na(MEDI_chest) | is.na(MEDI_wrist),
                       NA, x)
                }
              )
              )

Combine light exposure data with log and diary data
For the sleepdiary, a selection of sleep and wake times will be added. As the variable sleepprep (preparation for sleep) is the more reasonable time indicator for when the device positions are set for the night, this variable will be used instead of the calculated time of sleep (sleepprep + sleepdelay). For the wearlog, the start and end times of a removal, as well as the type (state) of removal will be used.

Preparation



Prepare sleepdiaries and wearlog for merging

sleepdiary_adj <-
  sleepdiary |>
  map(\(x) x |>
        select(Id, sleepprep, wake) |>
        group_by(Id) |>
        pivot_longer(-Id, names_to = "sleep", values_to = "Datetime") |>

        mutate(sleep = case_when(is.na(sleep) & State.Brown == "pre-sleep" ~ "wake",

title: Preparation of light exposure data for contextual analysis of placement errors
text:
This document describes the preparation of eye-level and body-worn dosimeter measurements for a statistical analysis which investigates whether contextual factors significantly affect the differences between light measurements at eye-level and on the body (chest and wrist), referred to as the placement error.
The dosimeter measurements were collected at multiple sites as part of the MeLiDos project, following the protocol of Guidolin et al. (Guidolin et al. 2024). The dataset of each site is available on GitHub:

BAUA, Dortmund, Germany (Broszio et al. 2025)
FUSPCEU, Madrid, Spain (Baeza Moyano et al. 2025)
IZTECH, Izmir, Turkey (Didikoglu et al. 2025)
KNUST, Kumasi, Ghana (Akuffo et al. 2025)
MPI, Tübingen, Germany (Guidolin et al. 2025)1
RISE, Borås, Sweden (Nilsson Tengelin et al. 2026)
THUAS, the Hague, the Netherlands (Aerts et al. 2025)
TUM, Munich, Germany (Hilden et al. 2025)
UCR, San Pedro, San José, Costa Rica (Sancho-Salas et al. 2026)

Each dataset contains dosimeter measurements from three body positions (eye level, chest, and wrist) alongside contextual data. These datasets were previously checked for gaps and irregularities, trimmed to only include measurements during the trial period, and adjusted to account for (if any) daylight saving time transitions.
All datasets were imported in R using the MelidosData library. Measurements at the three body positions were temporally aligned using LightLogR’s data2reference() function (Zauner et al. 2025), and only observations (time points) with simultaneous data from all three dosimeters were retained. Measurements during sleep (derived from Sleepdiaries.RData (“sleepprep” and “out_ofbed”)) or non-wear (derived from Wearlog.RData (“Start” and “end”)) were removed. Additionally, measurements above 100,000 lx melanopic EDI were removed, as these are outside of the dosimeter’s operating range.
Placement errors were calculated as log-transformed differences (logdif_x = log10(MEDI_x + 0.1) - log10(MEDI_h + 0.1)), where x refers to either the chest (c) or wrist (w) dosimeter. The offset of 0.1 is to avoid taking the logarithm of zero. As this offset lies below the dosimeter’s operating range, it has no meaningful impact on the results. Since the contextual data were gathered at an hourly resolution, the placement errors were aggregated to hourly means.
Three participants had one of the dosimeters recording at a non-standard sampling interval: FUSPCEU_S014 (head dosimeter at a 60-second interval), IZTECH_S016 (wrist dosimeter at a 120-second interval), and RISE_S011 (head dosimeter at a 1-second interval). These were still included, as enough data remained for calculating hourly means. Days with flat (zero) signals across all three dosimeters were removed for participants FUSPCEU_S010 (03-11-2024), FUSPCEU_S017 (09-12-2024), IZTECH_S009 (18-03-2025 and 19-03-2025), and THUAS_S007 (11-04-2025).

section: 2 Function to count participants and participant-days
text:
2 Function to count participants and participant-days
This function is executed at multiple points in the script to count the number of participants and participant-days remaining after each processing step. The resulting counts are presented in Table 1.

#| label: define-counter

# Initialize collector once
participant_stats <- list()

count_participants <- function(processing_step, data) {
  
  # Combine the datasets
  data <- bind_rows(data)
  
  result <- tibble(
    step = processing_step,
    participants = n_distinct(data$Id),
    participant_days = nrow(distinct(ungroup(data), Id, date = as_date(Datetime)))
  )
  
  participant_stats[[processing_step]] <<- result
  
  invisible(result) # Do not print results when calling the function
}

4 Combine measurements

#| label: combine-measurements

# Set timestamps of the chest and wrist measurements equal to the head measurements
combine_positions <- function(data) {
  h_data <- data |> filter(position == "h")
  c_data <- data |> filter(position == "c")
  w_data <- data |> filter(position == "w")
  
  data2reference(h_data, Reference.data = c_data, Reference.column = MEDI_c) |>
    left_join(
      data2reference(h_data, Reference.data = w_data, Reference.column = MEDI_w) |>
        select(Id, Datetime, MEDI_w),
      by = c("Id", "Datetime")) |>
    rename(MEDI_h = MEDI) |>
    select(-position)
}

datasets <- map(datasets, combine_positions)

#| label: combine-measurements

# Remove observations where one or more MEDI value is missing
na_summary <- imap(datasets, function(data, name) {
  incomplete <- !complete.cases(data)
  n_before <- nrow(data)
  n_removed <- sum(incomplete)
  
  tibble(
    site = name,
    n_before = n_before,
    n_after = n_before - n_removed,
    n_removed = n_removed,
    pct_removed = n_removed / n_before * 100
  )
}) |> list_rbind()

# Apply the filtering to each dataset in the list

  gt(rowname_col = "site") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(n_before, n_after, n_removed),

  fmt_number(columns = pct_removed, decimals = 1, pattern = "{x}%") |>
  cols_label(
    n_before = "Before",

#| label: visualize-light-data

vis_data <- function(data) {
  plot_data <- data |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("MEDI_"),
      names_to = "position",
      values_to = "MEDI"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      position = sub("^MEDI_", "", position),
      position = case_when(
        position == "h" ~ "head",
        position == "c" ~ "chest",
        position == "w" ~ "wrist"
      ),
      position = factor(position, levels = c("head", "chest", "wrist"))
    ) |>
    # Insert NA rows at gaps larger than 10 minutes
    # This is so geom line can be used, without having a continuous line through the night
    # (as geom line is much faster than geom point)
    arrange(Id, position, Datetime) |>
    group_by(Id, position) |>
    mutate(gap_break = as.numeric(difftime(Datetime, lag(Datetime), units = "mins")) > 10) |>
    mutate(MEDI = if_else(gap_break, NA_real_, MEDI)) |>
    select(-gap_break) |>
    group_by(Id)
  
  gg_days(
    dataset = plot_data,
    aes_col = position,
    geom = "line",
    alpha = 0.6,
    x.axis.limits = \(x) Datetime_limits(x, length = ddays(10))
  ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = pos_colors)
}

8.2 Format simplified activities
To decrease the number of combinations, the data is formatted (act_context column) into general categories deemed representative of the various activity contexts:

home (act_home)
working_indoor (act_working_indoor)
road_vehicle (act_road_vehicle)
outdoor_act (act_free_outdoor or act_road_open or act_working_outdoor or act_road_open and act_working_outdoor or act_road_open and act_free_outdoor)
other_act (Any other category or combination)

Additionally, the activity boolean columns are dropped from the datasets, as they are no longer needed.

#| label: activity-format

add_act_context <- function(data) {
  data |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(
      act_context = case_when(
        act_home == TRUE &
          act_sleep == FALSE & act_road_vehicle == FALSE & act_road_open == FALSE &
          act_working_indoor == FALSE & act_working_outdoor == FALSE &
          act_free_outdoor == FALSE & act_other == FALSE ~ "home",
        act_working_indoor == TRUE &
          act_sleep == FALSE & act_home == FALSE & act_road_vehicle == FALSE &
          act_road_open == FALSE & act_working_outdoor == FALSE &
          act_free_outdoor == FALSE & act_other == FALSE ~ "working_indoor",
        act_road_vehicle == TRUE &
          act_sleep == FALSE & act_home == FALSE & act_road_open == FALSE &
          act_working_indoor == FALSE & act_working_outdoor == FALSE &
          act_free_outdoor == FALSE & act_other == FALSE ~ "road_vehicle",
        (act_free_outdoor == TRUE &
          act_sleep == FALSE & act_home == FALSE & act_road_vehicle == FALSE &
          act_road_open == FALSE & act_working_indoor == FALSE &
          act_working_outdoor == FALSE & act_other == FALSE) |
        (act_free_outdoor == FALSE &
          act_sleep == FALSE & act_home == FALSE & act_road_vehicle == FALSE &
          act_road_open == TRUE & act_working_indoor == FALSE &
          act_working_outdoor == FALSE & act_other == FALSE) |
        (act_free_outdoor == FALSE &
          act_sleep == FALSE & act_home == FALSE & act_road_vehicle == FALSE &
          act_road_open == FALSE & act_working_indoor == FALSE &
          act_working_outdoor == TRUE & act_other == FALSE) |
        (act_free_outdoor == FALSE &
          act_sleep == FALSE & act_home == FALSE & act_road_vehicle == FALSE &
          act_road_open == TRUE & act_working_indoor == FALSE &
          act_working_outdoor == TRUE & act_other == FALSE) |
        (act_free_outdoor == TRUE &
          act_sleep == FALSE & act_home == FALSE & act_road_vehicle == FALSE &
          act_road_open == TRUE & act_working_indoor == FALSE &
          act_working_outdoor == FALSE & act_other == FALSE) ~ "outdoor_act",
        TRUE ~ "other_act"
      ),
      act_context = factor(act_context, levels = c(
        "home", "working_indoor", "road_vehicle", "outdoor_act", "other_act"
      ))
    ) |>
    select(-c(act_sleep, act_home, act_road_vehicle, act_road_open,
              act_working_indoor, act_working_outdoor, act_free_outdoor, act_other))
}

datasets <- map(datasets, add_act_context)



8.3 Format indoor work lighting categories
A column (work_light_context) was added to describe the primary light source when participants were working indoors. For observations where this was not the case, the column is set to NA. Additionally, the primary and secondary light source columns are dropped from the datasets, as they are no longer needed.

11 Data overview
The distributions of the differences between (hourly mean) log-transformed eye-level and body-worn dosimeters measurements (logdif_c and logdif_w)) during daytime, nighttime, indoor, and outdoor conditions are given in Figure 1 to Figure 4.

#| label: fig-2d-dis-func

make_hcw_plot <- function(data, filter_expr) {
  
  ALL_hcw <- data |>
    filter({{ filter_expr }}) |>
    select(Id, MEDI_h, MEDI_c, MEDI_w)

  # Non-zero / zero splits
  ALL_hc <- ALL_hcw |> filter(MEDI_h != 0, MEDI_c != 0) |> mutate(across(c(MEDI_h, MEDI_c), log10))
  ALL_hw <- ALL_hcw |> filter(MEDI_h != 0, MEDI_w != 0) |> mutate(across(c(MEDI_h, MEDI_w), log10))
  ALL_h0_c <- ALL_hcw |> filter(MEDI_h == 0, MEDI_c != 0) |> mutate(MEDI_c = log10(MEDI_c)) |> select(MEDI_c)
  ALL_h0_w <- ALL_hcw |> filter(MEDI_h == 0, MEDI_w != 0) |> mutate(MEDI_w = log10(MEDI_w)) |> select(MEDI_w)
  ALL_h_c0 <- ALL_hcw |> filter(MEDI_c == 0, MEDI_h != 0) |> mutate(MEDI_h = log10(MEDI_h)) |> select(MEDI_h)
  ALL_h_w0 <- ALL_hcw |> filter(MEDI_w == 0, MEDI_h != 0) |> mutate(MEDI_h = log10(MEDI_h)) |> select(MEDI_h)
  ALL_h0_c0 <- ALL_hcw |> filter(MEDI_h == 0, MEDI_c == 0)
  ALL_h0_w0 <- ALL_hcw |> filter(MEDI_h == 0, MEDI_w == 0)

  # Binning
  binwidth <- 0.2

  bin_2d <- function(df, v1, v2) {
    df |> ungroup() |>
      mutate(
        "{v1}_bin" := floor(.data[[v1]] / binwidth) * binwidth,
        "{v2}_bin" := floor(.data[[v2]] / binwidth) * binwidth
      )
  }

  bin_1d <- function(df, v) {
    df |> ungroup() |>
      mutate("{v}_bin" := floor(.data[[v]] / binwidth) * binwidth)
  }

  ALL_hc_bins <- bin_2d(ALL_hc, "MEDI_h", "MEDI_c")
  ALL_hw_bins <- bin_2d(ALL_hw, "MEDI_h", "MEDI_w")
  ALL_h0_c_bins <- bin_1d(ALL_h0_c, "MEDI_c")
  ALL_h0_w_bins <- bin_1d(ALL_h0_w, "MEDI_w")
  ALL_h_c0_bins <- bin_1d(ALL_h_c0, "MEDI_h")
  ALL_h_w0_bins <- bin_1d(ALL_h_w0, "MEDI_h")

  # Counts
  clamp_low <- function(df, ...) {
    vars <- ensyms(...)
    df |>
      mutate(across(c(!!!vars), \(x) ifelse(x < 0, -0.2, x))) |>
      group_by(across(c(!!!vars))) |>
      summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop")
  }

  ALL_hc_bins_counts <- ALL_hc_bins  |> count(MEDI_h_bin, MEDI_c_bin, name = "n") |> clamp_low(MEDI_h_bin, MEDI_c_bin)
  ALL_hw_bins_counts <- ALL_hw_bins  |> count(MEDI_h_bin, MEDI_w_bin, name = "n") |> clamp_low(MEDI_h_bin, MEDI_w_bin)
  ALL_h0_c_bins_counts <- ALL_h0_c_bins |> count(MEDI_c_bin, name = "n") |> clamp_low(MEDI_c_bin)
  ALL_h0_w_bins_counts <- ALL_h0_w_bins |> count(MEDI_w_bin, name = "n") |> clamp_low(MEDI_w_bin)
  ALL_h_c0_bins_counts <- ALL_h_c0_bins |> count(MEDI_h_bin, name = "n") |> clamp_low(MEDI_h_bin)
  ALL_h_w0_bins_counts <- ALL_h_w0_bins |> count(MEDI_h_bin, name = "n") |> clamp_low(MEDI_h_bin)
  ALL_h0_c0_count <- ALL_h0_c0 |> ungroup() |> count(MEDI_h, name = "n")
  ALL_h0_w0_count <- ALL_h0_w0 |> ungroup() |> count(MEDI_h, name = "n")

  # Shared fill scale
  global_min <- min(ALL_hc_bins_counts$n, ALL_hw_bins_counts$n,
                    ALL_h0_c_bins_counts$n, ALL_h0_w_bins_counts$n,
                    ALL_h_c0_bins_counts$n, ALL_h_w0_bins_counts$n,
                    ALL_h0_c0_count$n, ALL_h0_w0_count$n)
  global_max <- max(ALL_hc_bins_counts$n, ALL_hw_bins_counts$n,
                    ALL_h0_c_bins_counts$n, ALL_h0_w_bins_counts$n,
                    ALL_h_c0_bins_counts$n, ALL_h_w0_bins_counts$n,
                    ALL_h0_c0_count$n, ALL_h0_w0_count$n)
  log_breaks <- 10^seq(floor(log10(5)), ceiling(log10(global_max)), by = 1)

  fill_scale <- scale_fill_viridis_c(
    trans = "log10", option = "plasma", name = "Count",
    limits = c(global_min, global_max),
    breaks = log_breaks, labels = label_number()
  )

  # Layout design
  design <- c(
    area(t = 1, l = 1, b = 1, r = 1),
    area(t = 1, l = 2, b = 1, r = 2),
    area(t = 2, l = 1, b = 2, r = 1),
    area(t = 2, l = 2, b = 2, r = 2)
  )

  # Plot builder helpers
  tick_segments <- function(positions, axis, direction, offset = 0.2) {
    # axis: "x" or "y", direction: "in" or "out"
    if (axis == "x") {
      y_base <- if (direction == "out") 0 else positions[length(positions)] + offset
      y_tip  <- if (direction == "out") -offset else positions[length(positions)]
      df <- data.frame(x = positions, xend = positions,
                       y = if (direction == "out") 0 else 5.2,
                       yend = if (direction == "out") -offset else 5)
    } else {
      df <- data.frame(y = positions, yend = positions,
                       x = if (direction == "out") 0 else 5.2,
                       xend = if (direction == "out") -offset else 5)
    }
    geom_segment(data = df, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.6)
  }

  make_main_plot <- function(counts, x_bin, y_bin) {
    ggplot() +
      geom_rect(data = counts,
                aes(xmin = .data[[x_bin]], xmax = .data[[x_bin]] + binwidth,
                    ymin = .data[[y_bin]], ymax = .data[[y_bin]] + binwidth,
                    fill = n)) +
      coord_fixed() +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.2, 5.2), expand = c(0,0),
                         breaks = seq(0, 5), labels = NULL) +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.2, 5.2), expand = c(0,0),
                         breaks = seq(0, 5), labels = NULL) +
      fill_scale +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "black",
                  linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)) +
      # tick marks
      geom_segment(data = data.frame(x=seq(0,5), xend=seq(0,5), y=0, yend=-0.2),
                   aes(x=x,xend=xend,y=y,yend=yend), inherit.aes=FALSE, linewidth=0.6) +
      geom_segment(data = data.frame(y=seq(0,5), yend=seq(0,5), x=0, xend=-0.2),
                   aes(x=x,xend=xend,y=y,yend=yend), inherit.aes=FALSE, linewidth=0.6) +
      geom_segment(data = data.frame(x=seq(0,5), xend=seq(0,5), y=5.2, yend=5),
                   aes(x=x,xend=xend,y=y,yend=yend), inherit.aes=FALSE, linewidth=0.6) +
      geom_segment(data = data.frame(y=seq(0,5), yend=seq(0,5), x=5.2, xend=5),
                   aes(x=x,xend=xend,y=y,yend=yend), inherit.aes=FALSE, linewidth=0.6) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Count")
  }

  make_h0_plot <- function(counts, x_bin, x_lab) {
    ggplot() +
      geom_rect(data = counts,
                aes(xmin = .data[[x_bin]], xmax = .data[[x_bin]] + binwidth,
                    ymin = 0, ymax = binwidth, fill = n)) +
      coord_fixed() +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.2, 5.2), expand = c(0,0),
                         breaks = seq(0, 5),
                         labels = function(x) label_number(accuracy=1)(10^x)) +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, binwidth), expand = c(0,0),
                         breaks = binwidth/2, labels = NULL) +
      fill_scale + guides(fill = "none") +
      labs(x = x_lab, y = NULL) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
            panel.grid = element_blank()) +
      geom_segment(data = data.frame(x=seq(0,5), xend=seq(0,5), y=0, yend=0.2),
                   aes(x=x,xend=xend,y=y,yend=yend), inherit.aes=FALSE,
                   linewidth=0.6, color="black")
  }

  make_c0_plot <- function(counts, y_lab) {
    ggplot() +
      geom_rect(data = counts,
                aes(xmin = 0, xmax = binwidth,
                    ymin = MEDI_h_bin, ymax = MEDI_h_bin + binwidth, fill = n)) +
      coord_fixed() +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, binwidth), expand = c(0,0),
                         breaks = binwidth/2, labels = NULL) +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.2, 5.2), expand = c(0,0),
                         breaks = seq(0, 5),
                         labels = function(x) label_number(accuracy=1)(10^x)) +
      fill_scale + guides(fill = "none") +
      labs(x = NULL, y = y_lab) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
            panel.grid = element_blank()) +
      geom_segment(data = data.frame(x=0, xend=0.2, y=seq(0,5), yend=seq(0,5)),
                   aes(x=x,xend=xend,y=y,yend=yend), inherit.aes=FALSE,
                   linewidth=0.6, color="black")
  }

  make_h0c0_plot <- function(counts) {
    ggplot() +
      geom_rect(data = counts,
                aes(xmin=0, xmax=binwidth, ymin=0, ymax=binwidth, fill=n)) +
      coord_fixed() +
      scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,binwidth), expand=c(0,0), breaks=binwidth/2, labels=0) +
      scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,binwidth), expand=c(0,0), breaks=binwidth/2, labels=0) +
      fill_scale + guides(fill = "none") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour="black", fill=NA, linewidth=1),
            panel.grid = element_blank())
  }

  # Assemble the two composite plots
  plot_headvschest <- (
    make_c0_plot(ALL_h_c0_bins_counts, "Eye-level dosimeter [m-EDI lx]") +
    make_main_plot(ALL_hc_bins_counts, "MEDI_c_bin", "MEDI_h_bin") +
    make_h0c0_plot(ALL_h0_c0_count) +
    make_h0_plot(ALL_h0_c_bins_counts, "MEDI_c_bin", "Chest-worn dosimeter [m-EDI lx]")
  ) + plot_layout(design = design)

  plot_headvswrist <- (
    make_c0_plot(ALL_h_w0_bins_counts, NULL) +
    make_main_plot(ALL_hw_bins_counts, "MEDI_w_bin", "MEDI_h_bin") +
    make_h0c0_plot(ALL_h0_w0_count) +
    make_h0_plot(ALL_h0_w_bins_counts, "MEDI_w_bin", "Wrist-worn dosimeter [m-EDI lx]")
  ) + plot_layout(design = design)

  (plot_headvschest | plot_headvswrist) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") 
  }

summarise_by_category <- function(data, category_col, drop_na = FALSE) {
  category_col <- ensym(category_col)
  
  data <- data |> ungroup()
  if (drop_na) {
    data <- data |> filter(!is.na(!!category_col))
  }
  
  obs <- data |>
    count(!!category_col, name = "n_observations") |>
    mutate(perc_observations = n_observations / sum(n_observations) * 100)
  
  participants <- data |>
    distinct(!!category_col, Id) |>
    count(!!category_col, name = "n_participants")
  
  left_join(obs, participants, by = as_string(category_col))
}

format_summary_gt <- function(summary_df, category_col, title) {
  summary_df |>
    gt(rowname_col = category_col) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(n_observations, n_participants),
               decimals = 0, sep_mark = ",") |>
    fmt_number(columns = perc_observations, decimals = 1, pattern = "{x}%") |>
    cols_label(
      n_observations = "Observations",
      perc_observations = "% observations",
      n_participants = "Participants"
    ) |>
    tab_footnote(
      footnote = "Number of unique participants in subset.",
      locations = cells_column_labels(columns = n_participants)
    ) |>
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = list(cells_stub(), cells_column_labels())
    ) |>
    tab_header(title = title)
}
